title: You Think Cats Solve Door Latches by Logic, Yet Stopwatch Curves Proved Blind Reward
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — Edward Thorndike (1898): Wooden Puzzle Boxes, Escaping Cats & the Birth of the Law of Effect, grounded in Edward L. Thorndike (1898) (Animal intelligence: An experimental study of the associative processes in animals). Empirical findings show that before 1898, 'animal psychology' relied on charming Victorian fireside anecdotes ('My clever terrier understands door locks like a little gentleman!'). At age 23, Edward Thorndike nailed together 15 homemade wooden crate 'puzzle boxes' out of old packing slats and brought a stopwatch.

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: When Harvard administrators refused lab space for animals, William James hosted Thorndike's first chicks in the basement of the James family home in Cambridge before James McKeen Cattell gave Thorndike an attic lab at Columbia.
